play-introduction.text: Welcome to Billiards Play. Your table. Your friends. Your kind of game. Click or tap a game to explore it, then choose Start game. On a phone or tablet, tapping a game opens its setup straight away. Add your players, read the house rules, or tap the speaker to hear them in Chase’s voice. When everyone is ready, rack them up and use Play to keep score at your real table. Table tools adds drill tracking, a shot clock, and controls for compatible remotes. My player opens your own player view. Local table connects player phones when you are running a supported host. Tournament Play helps you organize a tournament night. You can return here whenever you want, resume a saved game from the bottom right, or clear it and start fresh. Pick a game, bring everyone together, and enjoy your next session.

rules-killer.text: Killer. Three lives. One shot per turn. Make a ball to stay safe; miss or foul to lose one life. Last player alive wins. A dry break gets one retry; a break scratch loses a life immediately. Rerack when empty. No eight-ball bonus in this version.

Enter the player names, separated by commas. Play the shots at your real pool table and record the results here. Choose Rack them up to begin, or Start new game if another game is saved. Starting a new game replaces the saved game.

rules-poker.text: Poker Pool. Five rounds, one shot each. Miss or foul: receive one random card. Make a legal pot: privately choose one of two cards. Multi-pots still earn one choice. After five full rounds, the best five-card poker hand wins. Equal hands tie; suits do not break ties. Rerack when empty. A legal break needs a pot or four object balls to cushions; one dry illegal-break retry is free.

rules-cutthroat.text: Cutthroat. Protect your five balls: 1–5, 6–10 or 11–15. Keep shooting after any legal pot, even your own. Losing your last ball ends your turn. Scratch: pots stay down, then one pocketed ball per opponent returns, bringing eliminated players back. Other foul pots return. Last surviving group wins after returns. If everyone goes out together, return one ball per group and continue.

rules-ghost.text: Ghost Runout. Break, take cue ball anywhere, then clear in numerical contact order. Break pots count and break scratches are forgiven. First post-break miss or foul gives the rack to the ghost. Clear to win it yourself. Race to five. Highest ball made early returns until last. Any full break clearance wins a rack.

rules-kelly.text: Kelly Pool. Lowest ball first. Keep shooting after a legal pot. Pot your own secret number to win. If someone else removes it, you receive a new available number for future shots. If no unassigned number remains, everyone gets a fresh rack and assignment. Foul pots return.

rules-blackjack.text: Twenty-One (Blackjack). Three hands. Start with two private cards. Stand at any time, or shoot: a legal pot draws one card, a miss stands, a foul busts. Aces count 1 or 11; faces count 10. Twenty-one stands automatically. Highest non-busted total wins a hand point; ties each score. Most hand points wins.

rules-cribbage.text: Cribbage Pool. Pairs 1+14 through 7+8 score one point each. Any unmatched ball you pot becomes an obligation: pot at least one owed partner on your next shot or return every held ball and end your turn. A foul also returns held balls and foul pots. Completed pairs stay scored. Ball 15 scores one only after all pairs are complete; early 15 returns. First to five wins; a final 4–4 is a draw.

rules-bingo.text: Billiards Bingo. Nine public shot tasks in shuffled positions per player. Choose an unmarked square and take one attempt on its reset layout. A success marks it. A completed line wins at the end of the full round, allowing joint winners. After ten rounds most marks wins. Bank and kick tasks require the named route; draw and follow require the cue ball to finish in the described zone.

rules-battleship.text: Battleship Billiards. Each player privately locks a hidden three-cell ship and two-cell ship on a 3×3 grid. A legal pot earns one attack, regardless of ball count. Choose an untried enemy cell, then pass. Miss or foul passes without attack. Sink all five enemy cells to win. Reracks preserve fleets.

rules-golf.text: Golf Pool. Six holes visit TL, TM, TR, BR, BM, BL. Each player starts each hole with cue ball at the head spot and one object ball at center. Pot it in the named pocket. Every stroke counts; a wrong pocket adds one, a scratch adds two, another foul adds one (only the largest penalty applies). Reset after wrong pocket or foul. Ten-stroke cap per hole. Lowest six-hole total wins.

rules-saboteur.text: Undercover Saboteur. Four rounds, one shot each. One secret saboteur wants the crew to miss a quota of twice the player count. Each legal scoring stroke adds one, including the saboteur’s pots. After round two everyone privately votes once, or abstains. A strict majority naming the saboteur adds one bonus at the final reveal. No early role reveal. Crew reaches quota to win; otherwise the saboteur wins.

rules-horse.text: H-O-R-S-E. The leader chooses a shot from the shared shot bank and attempts it. Failure passes leadership without a letter. Success makes every surviving opponent attempt the identical reset layout once. Each failure adds a letter; five letters eliminates. Leadership then advances. Last survivor wins.

rules-equalizer.text: Equalizer. Five shared three-ball layouts. Both players attempt each layout, alternating who starts. Setup assigns each player zero, one or two allowed misses and an optional cue-ball reset per layout. Pot all three before exceeding misses to score a point; any foul ends the attempt. Most cleared layouts wins. Allowances are visible and fixed for the match.

rules-bowliards.text: Bowliards. Ten bowling frames per player, two scoring visits per frame. A visit continues while you pot; miss or foul ends it. Foul pots return. Each fresh ten-ball rack starts with a free break: all break pots return, no points or penalties. Clear in visit one for a strike, visit two for a spare. Bowling bonuses use the next two or one visit totals. Frame ten grants two bonus visits after a strike or one after a spare; rerack whenever a bonus begins with an empty table. Highest bowling total wins.

rules-three.text: Three-Ball. Three rounds. Each player gets a fresh three-ball rack. Every stroke, including the break, counts one. A foul adds one extra and returns its pots. Six-stroke cap per attempt. Clear all three or reach the cap, then pass. Lowest total over three attempts wins.

rules-speed.text: Speed Pool. Two attempts per player. Clock starts on the break and stops when the last legal ball drops. Each foul adds ten seconds and returns its pots. Real-table mode uses Start, Penalty and Finish controls with a witness. Pausing or leaving an active attempt marks it interrupted; it cannot set a winning time. Each player’s best valid time competes; lowest wins.

rules-highlow.text: High-Low. One player must contact the lowest remaining ball first, the other the highest. Any legal pot scores one per ball and keeps the turn. Foul pots return. First to eight takes the rack. Swap low/high roles and alternate the breaker each rack. Best of three racks wins.

house-rules.text: A foul takes priority over a made ball. Unless this game says otherwise, foul-shot balls return and the next player gets cue ball anywhere. In real-table mode, report the result honestly; Undo corrects mistakes.

table-tools.text: Table tools. Pair a keyboard-style Bluetooth remote in your device settings, then assign its buttons and enable clicker mode. Voice commands begin with Table, followed by a command. Offline voice needs a supported Android Play app. The shot clock is controlled by the host. Set the shot length and extension allowance, then start the clock. Each recorded shot resets it. Expiry announces time without automatically declaring a foul. For drills, enter one player or a group, choose attempts per set and the number of sets, then start the drill. Record each attempt as made or missed. Play tracks results and rotates players when their set is complete. Guided table calibration helps you measure your cloth and cushions. Use Back to table at the top or bottom to return to the game choices, or tap outside this window to return to where you were.

clicker-help.text: Pair a keyboard-style Bluetooth remote in your device settings. Assign each button here, then enable it. The Android Play app can also capture external media or volume buttons while clicker mode is active. Browser support depends on the remote. Voice commands start with Table: ready, ball one made, miss, foul, scratch, undo, pause, resume, start clock, pause clock, extension, drill made, drill miss. Audio on enables referee announcements.

clock-help.text: The host owns the clock. Each shot resets it; extensions are limited per player for this match. Expiry announces time without automatically declaring a foul. Set seconds per shot, extension seconds, and extensions per player, then select Set clock. Use Start to run it, Pause clock to stop it, or Extension to use one of the current player’s extensions. Turn clock off removes it.

drill-help.text: Enter player names separated by commas. Choose the attempts per set and number of sets, then start a new drill. Record every attempt with Drill made or Drill miss. Each player completes their attempts before the next player takes over. Play shows each player’s made shots, attempts, and percentage. Undo drill attempt corrects the latest attempt in this session. Starting a new drill replaces the previous drill results.

host-seat-help.text: Choose your seat. This reserves it on the host; a phone assigned to that seat returns to waiting. Keep the screen facing you when opening a private view.

private-view-help.text: Turn the screen away from the room before revealing your private view. Hide it before passing the device. Private cards, targets, roles, fleets and votes are never read aloud by these instruction buttons.

foul-help.text: Report any balls made first if this game needs their numbers. Choose Scratch or Other foul to record the foul. Any selected balls are resolved with the foul as one shot. Cancel returns to the current game.

local-table-help.text: Host a local table from the Windows app or Android Play preview. Keep the host running and connect each player device to the same trusted private Wi-Fi. The network must allow devices to communicate. Players scan the invitation QR, enter a name, and wait for the host to approve their seat. A name alone never unlocks private cards. No internet is needed during local play. Sharing the current game invites players again. Ending sharing disconnects the players.

clear-game-help.text: Clear the saved game and its shot history to return to the game choices without a Resume game button. Connected player screens will be disconnected. This does not clear your drills, table-tool settings or tournament events.

calibration-overview.text: Measure your table. Use a clean ball and a level table. Film each trial side-on at sixty frames per second or faster with a measuring tape in view. Repeat each measurement at least three times, in both directions and on different cushions. These trials estimate rolling resistance and effective cushion response. They do not measure sliding friction, spin transfer, ball-ball throw, table level or pocket acceptance. Keep Trainer’s existing values for those.

calibration-cloth.text: Cloth resistance. Gently roll a ball without side spin. Start measuring only after it rolls smoothly. Measure from that point until the ball stops, clear of every cushion. Record travel distance in metres and time in seconds. Count video frames for timing; a hand stopwatch adds substantial error. Enter one trial per line: distance, then time.

calibration-cushion.text: Cushion response. Roll the ball squarely into a cushion with no side spin. From video, measure speed over short, equal windows immediately before and after impact. Enter the distance travelled in each window in metres. Use the same number of frames before and after. Avoid the impact frame, cushion compression and the first few frames of sliding after rebound; repeat at several gentle speeds. Enter one trial per line: incoming distance, then outgoing distance. The ratio of these distances estimates normal speed restitution. Rail-induced spin and cloth contact can bias it; this is a practical effective setting, not a laboratory cushion measurement.
